title: GONG: The Chuck Barris Story
summary: Hosts Josh and Chuck (Chuck Bryant, referred to as iHeart Intro/Chuck in transcript) profile Chuck Barris, the game show producer and host of The Gong Show, who is often wrongly credited with creating it. They cover his early career at NBC and ABC (including babysitting Dick Clark and his songwriting hit Palisades Park), his founding of Chuck Barris Productions and hit shows like The Dating Game, The Newlywed Game, and The Dollar a Dime-style Dollar Ninety Eight Beauty Show, the Gong Show's format and celebrity panel, the flop Three's a Crowd and its misogyny criticism, the 1980 Gong Show movie, his 1984 memoir Confessions of a Dangerous Mind claiming CIA assassinations, the 2002 CIA denial, the George Clooney film adaptation, and his 2017 death. The episode also includes a listener mail correction about ADHD medications.

segments.title: Opening banter and introduction to Chuck Barris
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the episode about Chuck Barris, who was wrongly credited with creating The Gong Show, and note his claimed CIA assassin memoir. Brief discussion of Woman of the Hour plug and why Barris was chosen.

segments.title: Early career: NBC, ABC, Dick Clark and songwriting
segments.summary: Barris was born in 1929 in Philadelphia, worked as a page at NBC, then at ABC was assigned to monitor Dick Clark on American Bandstand; his notes helped Clark in a payola inquiry. He wrote the song Palisades Park, recorded by Freddie Cannon.

segments.title: People Poker and founding Chuck Barris Productions
segments.summary: Barris became director of daytime programs at ABC, pitched People Poker, left ABC, and founded Chuck Barris Productions in 1965 with a loan from his stepdad.

segments.title: The Dating Game
segments.summary: The Dating Game, developed in 1965 and sold to ABC, became a hit; Jim Lange and later Chuck Woolery hosted, and early-career actors and Andy Kaufman appeared as contestants.

segments.title: Woman of the Hour plug
segments.summary: Hosts promote Anna Kendrick's Netflix film Woman of the Hour, about serial killer Rodney Alcala who appeared on The Dating Game.

segments.title: The Newlywed Game and Acapulco prizes
segments.summary: Barris produced The Newlywed Game with couples, with raunchy answers and cheap prizes; he reportedly chose couples with the same dream prize so losing hurt more.

segments.title: Dollar Ninety Eight Beauty Show and misogyny criticism
segments.summary: Barris produced a long run of shows including The Dollar Ninety Eight Beauty Show hosted by Rip Taylor, a spoof of pageants that mocked women and drew criticism for misogyny.

segments.title: Book writing: You and Me, Babe
segments.summary: Barris published the fictionalized marriage account You and Me, Babe in 1974, which reached the New York Times bestseller list, and hoped to be remembered as an author.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Transition break before the Gong Show segment.

segments.title: The Gong Show format and host style
segments.summary: The Gong Show, hosted by Barris starting in 1976, featured amateur acts judged by celebrity panelists who could hit the gong; the show was described as part talent show, part demented variety show. Barris hid behind hats and was awkward on air.

segments.title: Notable Gong Show performers
segments.summary: Oingo Boingo, Boxcar Willie, Paul Reubens (as proto-Pee-Wee Herman), Cheryl Lynn, and a twelve-year-old Sandahl Bergman-era performer (Annie lead) appeared; Reubens credited the show for SAG minimum pay and exposure.

segments.title: Three's a Crowd and the decline; Gong Show movie
segments.summary: Barris's Three's a Crowd, which pitted wives against mistresses or secretaries, drew heavy criticism; NOW gave him a Golden Turkey-type award and UAW opposed it. He sold his company around 1980 and retreated. The 1980 Gong Show movie was a flop.

segments.title: Ringmaster and fictionalized real-life films
segments.summary: Hosts compare the Gong Show movie to Ringmaster, a Jerry Springer film, and joke about fictionalized versions of real jobs.

segments.title: Break before Act three
segments.summary: Transition break before the CIA assassin segment.

segments.title: Confessions of a Dangerous Mind and CIA assassin claims
segments.summary: The 1984 memoir Confessions of a Dangerous Mind claimed Barris was a CIA hitman with thirty-three murders. Critics read it as metaphor; Barris said on TV it was a character. The CIA spokesman Chris Bell denied it in 2002. The book sold poorly until Andrew Lazar revived it.

segments.title: Film adaptations: Clooney, Kaufman, Auto Focus
segments.summary: George Clooney directed the 2002 film with Sam Rockwell; Charlie Kaufman wrote an unproduced earlier script. Hosts discuss Kaufman and polished early-2000s films like Auto Focus and Catch Me If You Can.

segments.title: Barris's death, later books, and syndication
segments.summary: Barris died in 2017 at age 87 (age uncertain). He wrote Bad Grass Never Died in 2004. He created The Parent Game and sold it directly to stations, helping create syndication.

segments.title: Listener mail: ADHD medication correction
segments.summary: A pharmacist listener corrects the show's categorization of Strattera as an amphetamine-based stimulant; it is a non-stimulant SNRI. Hosts thank listeners for feedback.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts invite feedback by email and close the episode.
